title: Prerequisites for Learning Angular knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Prerequisites for Learning Angular”?
options: Prerequisites for Learning Angular should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Prerequisites for Learning Angular helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Prerequisites for Learning Angular means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Prerequisites for Learning Angular removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Prerequisites for Learning Angular helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Prerequisites for Learning Angular is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “HTML document structure” in this lesson?
options: Connect “HTML document structure” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “HTML document structure” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “HTML document structure” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “HTML document structure” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “HTML document structure” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “HTML document structure” under Prerequisites for Learning Angular. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Prerequisites for Learning Angular”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
